content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Karen Black (E008)
Request: admin access to Source Code

Team memory has two notes with conflicting information:

Note 1: role Payroll Specialist, employment type full_time, recommendation for Source Code: write
- Full-time employees can have up to write. Admin only if role owns system. Source Code is owned by Engineer role. Payroll Specialist doesn't own it, so admin not permitted. Max is write.

Note 2: role Payroll Specialist, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation: read
- Contractors: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Basic training max is read.

The two notes conflict on employment type. Note 2 says security record says contractor, note 1 listed full-time but apparently that was from HR? The security DB shows contractor.

As the Approver, I need to make a decision. The policy:
1. full_time: up to write; admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Either way, Karen does not own Source Code (she's a Payroll Specialist), so admin is not permitted. The maximum would be write (if full-time) or read (if contractor with basic training).

The requested level is admin, which is above the maximum in either case. So grant the maximum.

Which maximum applies? There's conflicting info. The security note says contractor with basic training, max read. The HR note says full-time, max write (since no ownership).

Hmm. The approver must decide. The notes both concern the same employee. Given conflicting records, what's the safest? The policy says never grant more than requested; request is admin, so we cap at max. The question is whether max is read or write.

Note 2 says the security record says contractor. Security is typically the authority on access. Also, the note explicitly says prior note listed full-time but security record says contractor. Since the team relies on notes, and the most recent/authoritative security info says contractor with basic training, max is read.

Also, considering the conflicting info, granting read is safer and consistent with the contractor classification. Grant read.

Let me submit decision: read.
